results.name: Planet_Impact
results.description:
**Introduction**
The origin of the Moon has long been attributed to impaction of Mars-sized body on the early Earth, ejecting debris into orbit that gradually coalesced into the Moon. However, such models struggle to account for the composition of the Moon.

A. Kegerreis et al. suggest a Moon-like satellite could form immediately after such a
giant impact. This project visualizes a similar planetary collision using SPH simulations and blender. 

Complete movie: https://youtu.be/lX9ML_c0m9M

**Method**
- Mass ratio of target : impactor = 5 : 1
- Material Composition:
  - Core: 30% of mass, composed of iron-silicate alloy
  - Mantle: 70% of mass, composed of forsterite
- Collision angle at 45 with mutual escape velocity
- Animainted by timeframe animation 

**Reference**
J. A. Kegerreis et al., “Immediate origin of the Moon as a post-impact satellite,”  doi:10.3847/2041-8213/ac8d96
M. Schaller et al., “SWIFT: SPH With Inter-dependent Fine-grained Tasking,” Astrophysics Source
Code Library, May 2018.
